answer: A wharf only stays trustworthy when every berth is vouched for by captains whose own standing is on the line: let each endorsement be like cedar, strong but slowly weathering, so vouches decay unless the voucher keeps behaving honestly, and let a voucher who backs a fake lose reputation and future vouching power. An opal seal that never fades would let one operator mint endless sock-puppets through a single old friend; decaying, stake-backed vouches force every new identity to keep earning fresh trust from distinct, still-reputable peers.
